correlation_note: This award's start date (2025-10-01) falls after event-simon-took-office (2025-01-03), roughly 9 months later. Flagged per issue #8's requirement to surface temporal proximity explicitly and mark it correlation_only rather than silently noting or silently ignoring it.

description: Rep. Simon elected to the BART Board of Directors, District 7. Exact election date approximated as the 2016 general election date; not independently confirmed against an official certified-results record.
source: Wikipedia and general web search corroboration, accessed 2026-10-03: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lateefah_Simon. Not yet verified against Alameda/Contra Costa/San Francisco County certified election results.

description: BART staff announced Simon's removal from the board over a residency dispute (her Oakland address was determined to be ~300 feet outside the District 7 boundary).

BART reversed the removal after outside counsel found staff lacked authority to remove an elected director; BART concluded Simon retained her seat without interruption throughout the dispute. Recorded as context: this confirms she was a sitting, undisputed director well before the 2022-12-01 North Berkeley TOD board action below, so that later vote is not clouded by this earlier, resolved dispute.

BART Board of Directors authorized the General Manager to enter a two-year Exclusive Negotiating Agreement (ENA) with BRIDGE Housing Corporation to plan a Transit-Oriented Development at the North Berkeley BART station (and, contingently, with Republic Metropolitan). BART's news release names then-Board-President Rebecca Saltzman and does NOT name Rep. Simon. Simon was a sitting District 7 director at this date (elected 2016, continuously per event-simon-bart-reinstated above). This item (Agenda Item 8-A) was heard under the Planning, Public Affairs, Access, and Legislation Committee, chaired by Director Foley -- NOT Simon's committee. The same day's agenda separately lists 'Director Simon, Chairperson' for Item 9 (Administration Items), confirming she was present/active in some capacity at this meeting, but that is a different agenda section from the North Berkeley ENA item and does not establish her presence, vote, or absence on 8-A specifically. Checked directly against BART's Legistar API (2026-10-04): the event item record for 8-A (EventItemId 21666, Matter 22-461) has EventItemRollCallFlag=0 and an empty votes array -- BART's own system has NO individually-recorded director vote for this item, consistent with passage by voice/consensus vote rather than an individual roll call. Contemporaneous reporting (Berkeleyside, 2022-12-01) describes Director Saltzman as vocally opposed ('pissed off'), indicating the vote was not unanimous, but no source found records how each individual director, including Simon, voted. This remains the most load-bearing, least-confirmed fact in this entire package: not because the search was incomplete, but because the primary record itself does not appear to capture individual votes on this item.
source: BART official news release, accessed 2026-10-03: https://www.bart.gov/news/articles/2022/news20221201; BART Board agenda, Dec. 1, 2022, fetched directly 2026-10-04: https://bart.legistar1.com/bart/meetings/2022/12/1289_A_Board_of_Directors_22-12-01_BOARD_MEETING_AGENDA.pdf; BART Legistar Web API, fetched directly 2026-10-04: https://webapi.legistar.com/v1/bart/eventitems/21666 and https://webapi.legistar.com/v1/bart/eventitems/21666/votes; Berkeleyside, 2022-12-01: https://www.berkeleyside.org/2022/12/01/north-berkeley-bart-housing-developer-bridge
correlation_note: This is the single most significant documented institutional fact linking BRIDGE Housing Corporation to an agency Rep. Simon sat on. It is NOT evidence of her personal involvement, vote, or any impropriety -- it is a board-level action by a multi-member elected body, during a period she was one of nine directors, on a routine real-estate planning authorization (an ENA is a negotiating framework, not a final contract award or public funds disbursement). A direct check of BART's own Legistar system (2026-10-04) found no individually-recorded vote for this item at all -- the roll-call-vote next step originally flagged in unresolved_leads.json has now been checked and found to not exist in the primary record, not merely unfetched. Absent a transcript or video review of the meeting audio (https://bart.gov/boardtv archive, not yet attempted), this fact cannot be resolved further from structured records.

description: Insight Housing, BRIDGE Housing Corporation, East Bay Asian Local Development Corporation (EBALDC), and AvalonBay Communities are reported as the development team ('North Berkeley Housing Partners') for the North Berkeley BART Transit-Oriented Development. This is the first and only documented institutional link between Insight Housing and BRIDGE Housing Corporation found in this investigation to date -- everything else in this package treated them as unrelated entities with only incidental Bay Area geographic overlap.
source: General web search corroboration of multiple outlets describing the North Berkeley TOD development team, accessed 2026-10-03. NOT yet independently verified against a primary BART project-page document or a signed partnership/JV filing naming all four entities together -- this is the single highest-priority item to verify with a primary source next.
